ops.title: Verify capt-hook end to end after every change, on both fleet hosts
ops.description:
capt-hook is the hook framework every Claude Code session in this fleet runs on. **It is the thing we absolutely cannot break.** Standing instruction: run this after every change that could plausibly touch it — daemonkit releases, captain-hook upgrades, plugin-cache changes, state-root work, anything that moves a binary or a LaunchAgent.

Run it on **both hosts**: this workstation and `yasyf-forge-studio` (`yasyf@100.113.56.52` over Tailscale).

## The one trap on forge-studio

Its login shell is **fish**, where an unmatched glob is an *error* rather than an empty expansion. That has already produced one badly wrong reading. Drive every remote command through a POSIX shell — `ssh yasyf@100.113.56.52 sh <<'SCRIPT' … SCRIPT` — and sanity-check the wrapper against a known-empty glob before trusting any count.

## What "verified" means

A session completing successfully is **not** proof. Hooks can silently fail to dispatch while the session looks perfectly healthy. The proof is `capt-hook heartbeats --session <id>` showing a populated event ledger for a session you just ran. Everything before that step is necessary but not sufficient.

## Reading the heartbeat ledger

A tool-using session shows the full spread — `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop`, `Stop`. A trivial headless session that runs no tools correctly shows only `SessionStart ×1`, `UserPromptSubmit ×1`, `Stop ×1`, `SessionEnd ×1` — **absent `PreToolUse` there is right, not a failure.** An empty ledger for any session is the failure.

A few `PostToolUseFailure` entries are normal; they track failed tool calls, not hook faults.

## Known-good baseline, 2026-08-29

- **This workstation**: all copies at **12.22.4** — Homebrew formula, deployed app, and the `capt-hook` uv tool on PATH. Host and helper both launchctl status 0. A live session showed 11 event types dispatching (`PreToolUse ×2890`, `PostToolUse ×2828`, `SubagentStart ×81`); a fresh headless session showed the clean 4-event lifecycle.
- **forge-studio**: deliberately at **12.22.3** while its Cellar is 12.22.4. This is a decided position, not drift — the deployment path that would converge it has a live drain bug that wedged the host once. Do not converge it during verification.

## Version split is a real failure mode

capt-hook exists in up to four places at once and nothing reports a disagreement: the Homebrew formula, the deployed `~/Applications/Captain Hook.app`, the `capt-hook` on PATH (a **uv tool**, which `brew upgrade` does not touch), and the Claude plugin cache under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/captain-hook/`. On 2026-08-29 this workstation had **three different versions simultaneously** — formula 12.22.4, uv shim 12.21.3, plugin cache 12.21.6 — and the stale uv shim's updater logged `update ok` twice while the host never moved. **Report each copy separately; never collapse them into one number.**

Converge the uv shim with `uv tool install --force 'capt-hook==<version>'`.

## If it is broken

A wedged host is **recoverable, not broken**: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.yasyf.captain-hook.host.v1` plus `launchctl kickstart gui/$UID/com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper` restores it, and a stale `daemon.records` entry clears itself on the next generation. Try that before anything heavier, and never reach for `package-install` as a repair — that is what wedged forge-studio.

ops.text: Health: `launchctl list | grep -E 'captain-hook|capt-hook'` — both `com.yasyf.captain-hook.host.v1` and `com.yasyf.capt-hook.helper` must report status 0.
Helper reachable: `capt-hook helper status` — expect `helper v<version> ok=True`. A connect errno 2 means the helper is down.

Version agreement — report all four separately, never as one number: Homebrew formula (`brew list --versions captain-hook`), deployed app (`defaults read ~/Applications/Captain\ Hook.app/Contents/Info.plist CFBundleShortVersionString`), the PATH shim (`uv tool list | grep capt-hook`), and the plugin cache (`ls ~/.claude/plugins/cache/captain-hook/captain-hook/`). A split is a finding.
Hook discovery: `capt-hook hooks` — must enumerate hooks across packs rather than erroring. Note the count and the packs.

Inline tests: `capt-hook test` in a repo carrying its own `.claude/hooks/`. 'No inline tests found' is a correct answer for a repo without them — pick one that has them before treating it as a signal.
THE ACTUAL PROOF — run a real session: `cd ~/Code/daemonkit && claude -p 'reply with exactly: ok'`.

Confirm dispatch: find that session's id (newest `~/.claude/projects/<project>/*.jsonl`) and run `capt-hook heartbeats --session <id>`. A populated ledger is the pass condition. An empty ledger means hooks silently did not fire — that is the failure this runbook exists to catch, and a clean session exit does not rule it out.

Worker health: re-check `capt-hookd status` after the session — confirm `workers` is sane and no worker died. A `TypeError` from a hook pack (e.g. cc-notes `record.py`) kills the worker without failing the session.
Repeat every step on forge-studio via an `ssh … sh <<'SCRIPT'` heredoc, wrapper sanity-checked against a known-empty glob first.
